observations: Initial longest-first jobs eight-four-two-one had total wait thirty-four.
Moving one-minute job earlier three times passed through wait thirty-three and twenty-three.
Shortest-first one-two-four-eight gave waiting zero-one-three-seven, total eleven; total execution remained fifteen.

Returning to longest-first before reveal did not lose original comparison. Reveal sums both cases, explains each front job delays all behind, and notes long-job starvation under continual short arrivals.

complexity.reason: Summed individual waiting differs from wall-clock completion.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Track multiplicative delay imposed by earlier jobs.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Four move-earlier buttons and two presets.

whyCool: Moving one long job later can remove its delay from everyone ahead of it without changing the total work.
caveat: Known fixed job durations, all available initially and no switching overhead; real arrival/fairness policy not simulated.
effort: Prediction, three local swaps, shortest preset, return to longest, screenshots and comparative reveal.
bucketReason: Highly manipulable scheduling mechanism with explicit starvation limit.

prediction.evidence: Same thirty-four, about third, or slightly less.

interaction.evidence: Several learner-chosen orders plus shortest and longest.

payoff.reason: Explains exact waiting sums, marginal delay mechanism and a meaningful limit.
payoff.evidence: Front job counted for every follower; continual short arrivals can starve long jobs.

clarity.reason: Shaded waiting versus colored execution separates unchanged work from changed wait.
clarity.evidence: Timeline still fifteen while total waiting changes.

transfer.reason: Concrete scheduling rule with objective and failure condition.
transfer.evidence: Minimize aggregate waiting for this batch; streaming arrivals can cause starvation.

surprise.reason: Same work can impose dramatically different summed delay.

visualExplanation.evidence: Moving a short job reduces many shaded intervals.

playfulness.reason: Learner can freely reorder via local swaps and compare presets.

depth.evidence: Optimal batch order need not be fair under continued arrivals.
